text: Biological systems inherently relational, governed complex interaction networks among genes, transcripts, proteins organisms. systematic organisation relational metadata within public repositories—UniProt (proteins), Rhea (reactions), KEGG (metabolic pathways)—provides foundational framework modern computational biology. However, leveraging resources routine bioinformatics workflows frequently hindered fragmented data structures, heterogeneous file formats data volumes exceed local computational capacities. Without structured approach, navigating labyrinth biological knowledge can feel overwhelming, time-consuming discouraging. ariadne addresses challenges assembling reproducible graph interlinked biological resources coupled robust programmatic toolkit, facilitates knowledge-driven annotation, feature stratification goal-oriented resource traversal. example, enables functional annotation microbial features via ChocoPhlAn Web Life (WoL), alongside feature aggregation using metabolic modules microbial signatures. naturally extending multi-omics modalities (e.g., metabolites, proteins genes), ariadne provides unified interface integrating prior biological knowledge standard Bioconductor workflows (example use cases presented vignette).

Agglomerate microbiome experiment by Genus mae[["microbiota"]] <- agglomerateByRank(mae[["microbiota"]], rank = "Genus") #> Duplicated labels were made unique.  # Remove rank prefix from taxon names rownames(mae[["microbiota"]]) <- mae[["microbiota"]] |>     rownames() |>     str_remove(fixed("D_5__"))  #
